ai.description: Anderson’s Pit Viper reaches 60–80 cm. It is typically bright green with a distinct reddish-brown tail and a thin, pale lateral stripe. A prominent white postocular stripe marks its triangular head.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Trimeresurus andersonii* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid yellow-green body featuring a distinct series of dark, reddish-brown or blackish crossbands along the back.
ai.habitat: Trimeresurus andersonii inhabits the dense tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, typically found in low-to-mid altitudinal zones.
ai.behavior: Anderson’s pit viper is primarily nocturnal, often positioning itself on low-hanging branches to ambush passing prey with a rapid strike.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trimeresurus andersonii* is viviparous, typically producing litters of 5–12 young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with births recorded between July and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trimeresurus andersonii* is endemic to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where it inhabits lowland tropical forests from sea level up to moderate elevations.
